images.caption:
Scope and content:  The original finding aid described this photograph as:
Original Caption: The "J" on the gate stands for Albert Johnson, a wealthy insurance man who funded one of Scotty's goldmines. The "S" stands for Walter Scott, better known as "Death Valley Scotty."
Location: California (37.032° N 117.341° W)

Status: Public domain. Photo from National Park Service

images.filename: Haystack for use at Death Valley Ranch, tarped from weather and fenced from livestock. Tonopah and Tidewater Railroad train (06596042-81c4-4b4e-a448-ccb39313e691).jpg
images.caption:
This is an historic black and white photograph from the Scotty's Castle Historic Photograph Collection, Death Valley National Park of haystack for use at Death Valley Ranch, tarped from weather and fenced from livestock. Tonopah and Tidewater Railroad train, last train to run on line north of Beatty, Nevada, arriving at Bonnie Clare station. January 7, 1928. Photographed by Mat Roy Thompson.
Haystack for use at Death Valley Ranch, tarped from weather and fenced from livestock. Tonopah and Tidewater Railroad train, last train to run on line north of Beatty, Nevada, arriving at Bonnie Clare station. January 7, 1928. Photographed by Mat Roy Thompson. Inscription in black ink, bottom center: Last Train-1-7-28. Number in black ink in left corner refers to historic photograph numbering system: 1622. Probably on reverse: G - refers to order of multiple photographs. In pencil, on reverse: 63.  Probably on reverse based on previous catalog card: Haystack (Castle supple) with water barrel on top (fire safety) next to track. Black and white, horizontal format, 3 x 5 inch. Corner mounted in photograph album.

images.filename: Carrie Lee Johnson playing with three puppies inside the chicken pen attached to Scotty's Castle Garage Long Shed Bunkhouse (0b212d70-eb20-4158-9e04-688a78a92177).jpg
images.caption:
This is an historic black and white photograph from the Scotty's Castle Historic Photograph Collection, Death Valley National Park of Carrie Lee Johnson playing with three puppies inside the chicken pen attached to Scotty's Castle Garage / Long Shed / Bunkhouse. May 27, 1928. Photographed by Mat Roy Thompson.
Carrie Lee Johnson playing with three puppies inside the chicken pen attached to Scotty's Castle Garage / Long Shed / Bunkhouse. May 27, 1928. Photographed by Mat Roy Thompson. Carrie's father, Norman, was Albert M. Johnson's first cousin. Johnson thought of her as his foster daughter. These may be Queenie's puppies, Walter Edward Perry Scott's dog. Inscription in black ink on lower left corner referring to historic photograph number system: 1663; date at bottom center: 5-27-28.  Black and white, 3x5 inch, vertical format. Corner mounted and glued in photograph album.

images.filename: Horse hobbled on ground to trim hooves by unidentified men. Albert M. Johnson holding a rope. Carrie Lee Johnson and Edna Devlin (ce72aad9-66b1-4cc9-a994-0de567992355).jpg
images.caption:
This is an historic black and white photograph from the Scotty's Castle Historic Photograph Collection, Death Valley National Park of Horse hobbled on ground to trim hooves by men. Albert M. Johnson holding a rope. Carrie Lee Johnson and Edna Devlin watching. April 23, 1928. Photographed by Mat Roy Thompson.
Horse hobbled on ground to trim hooves by unidentified men. Albert M. Johnson holding a rope. Carrie Lee Johnson and Edna Devlin watching. April 23, 1928. Photographed by Mat Roy Thompson. Men covering eyes and holding rasp to trim hoof. Looking northwest at Scotty's Castle Stables original northern section in background. Carrie's father, Norman, was Albert M. Johnson's first cousin. Johnson thought of her as his foster daughter. Devlin is Johnson's secretary. Inscription in black ink on lower left corner referring to historic photograph number system: 1695. Black and white, 3x5 inch, horizontal format. Corner mounted in photograph album.
